gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Jackery Explorer 300D, which ChatGPT carded at $199 with 'verify the exact USB-C port rating', has two 140 W USB-C ports plus a 65 W one, weighs 5.5 lb and sells for $209 on jackery.com today, or that the Explorer 300 v2 ChatGPT also carded is sold out at Jackery.
standout_why: I compared against the cited manuals.plus C300 DC guide and The Gadgeteer's C300 DC review, plus Amphourly's 'Best Small Portable Power Stations Under 500Wh'. The Gadgeteer covers only the Anker and names no rivals. Its $199.99 list and $139.99 sale prices date from November 2024. Amphourly lists the RIVER 3, RIVER 3 Plus, Elite 30 V2, Anker C300 (AC) and Jackery 300 Plus. It gives no prices except Anker's launch MSRP and does not cover the 300D or the TRAIL. ChatGPT's own answer told the shopper to check the 300D's USB-C rating and pointed them to a 300 v2 that Jackery lists as sold out.
decides: This confirms that a DC-only 288 Wh unit fits the question better than an AC station. The Jackery 300D (5.5 lb, 2× 140 W USB-C, $209 at Jackery) is now the lightest fully sourced, maker-priced option with more than 100 W of USB-C. It sits alongside the Anker C300 DC, whose US price I could not read today. Every station with an AC outlet costs more ($289–$289.99) and is heavier. The Jackery Explorer 300 (new) and EcoFlow RIVER 3 have only one 100 W USB-C port, and the RIVER 3 Plus is over 10 lb.
